p.docTitle:
Ordinance
on the Central Visa Information System and the National Visa System

preamble.p:
on the basis of Article 109e of the Foreign Nationals and Integration Act
of 16 December 2005
SR 142.20 (FNIA)
This title was revised on 1 Jan. 2019 pursuant to Art. 12 para. 2 of the Publications Act of 18 June 2004 (SR 170.512). The modification has been made throughout the text. ,

blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance regulates:

item.p: responsibility for the National Visa System (ORBIS) and its content;
the authorities' access rights to ORBIS;
the authorities' access rights to the Central Visa Information System (C‑VIS);
the procedure for transmitting C-VIS data via the central access point to the authorities under Articles 17 and 18;
the processing and the retention period for the data;
the rights of the persons concerned;
data security, advice on data protection and the supervision of data processing.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Ordinance:

item.p: third country means a state that is neither a member state of the European Union (EU) nor of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA);
Schengen state means a state bound by any one of the Schengen Association Agreements; these agreements are listed in Annex 1 number 1;
Dublin state means a state bound by any one of the Dublin Association Agreements; these agreements are listed in Annex 1 number 2;

item.num:
e.
Inserted by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2021, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 735).

f.
Inserted by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2021, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 735).
item.p: other serious offence means an offence under Annex 1b of the N-SIS Ordinance.

section.heading: Responsibility, Aim and Structure of the System

content.p:
The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM)
The name of this administrative unit was amended by Art. 16 para. 3 of the Publications O of 17 Nov. 2004 (AS 2004 4937), in force since 1 Jan. 2015. This amendment has been made throughout the text. is responsible for ORBIS.
It shall issue processing regulations, which in particular set out the measures required to guarantee data protection and data security.

blockList.listIntroduction: ORBIS has the following aims:

item.p: to record and store the data on visa applications;
to allow access to the C-VIS data.

content.p: ORBIS contains the data specified in Annex 2 relating to each admissible visa application.

The data recorded in ORBIS in application of the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. are transmitted automatically to the C-VIS.
All modifications and deletions of data recorded in ORBIS in application of the EU VIS Regulation are transmitted automatically via ORBIS to the C-VIS.

section.heading: Recording the Data and Transmission to the C-VIS

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No II of the O of 2 Sept. 2015, in force since 1 Oct. 2015 (AS 2015 3047).

article.heading: Electronic visa applications for Schengen visas and temporary storage of data

content.p: In the case of applications for Schengen visas, the applicant may send the personal data required for the application to the visa authority electronically.
The fees may be paid electronically.
The data under paragraph 1 may be stored on servers of the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) for a maximum of four months.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No II of the O of 2 Sept. 2015, in force since 1 Oct. 2015 (AS 2015 3047).

article.heading: Data processing by external service providers

content.p: The applicant may send the personal data required for the visa application to an external service provider that has been assigned tasks in connection with the visa procedure.

The external service provider shall record the personal data in compliance with the provisions of Annex X of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009
Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 July 2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas (Visa Code), OJ L 243 of 15.9.2009, p. 1; last amended by Regulation (EC) 2024/1415, OJ L 024/1415, 22.05.2024. (Visa Code) and shall pass these on to the visa authority.
Amended by No II 2 of the O of 7 June 2024, in force since 11 June 2024 (AS 2024 258).

article.heading:
Recording data in ORBIS by the visa authority
Amended by No II of the O of 2 Sept. 2015, in force since 1 Oct. 2015 (AS 2015 3047).

content.p:
If a visa application is admissible under Article 19 of the Visa Code
See footnote to Art. 5b para. 2.
Term in accordance with No I of the O of 5 April 2017, in force since 1 May 2017 (AS 2017 2551). This amendment has been made throughout the text. , the visa authorities shall record the data specified in Annex 2 in in ORBIS accordance with Articles 8–14 of the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. ; the data in Category I must be recorded first and thereafter, depending on the course of the procedure, the data in Categories II–VI.
Amended by No II of the O of 2 Sept. 2015, in force since 1 Oct. 2015 (AS 2015 3047).

If the application relates to a short-stay or airport transit visa, the data in Categories I–VI is transmitted to the C-VIS in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 2.
Amended by Art. 69 para. 2 No 3 of the O of 15 Aug. 2018 on Entry and the Issuing of Visas, in force since 15 Sept. 2018 (AS 2018 3087).
The visa authorities shall also record the data in Category VII listed in Annex 2. These data are not transmitted to the C-VIS.

article.heading: Recording on behalf of another Schengen state

content.p: If a Swiss authority records the data on a visa application on behalf of another Schengen state, it shall enter the name of the state concerned into ORBIS.

If the authority under paragraph 1 issues, refuses, revokes, annuls or extends a visa, or if it does not continue the assessment of the application, the name of the state concerned is transmitted automatically to the C-VIS.

article.heading: Owner the data transmitted to the C-VIS

content.p: Switzerland is the owner of the data entered by the Swiss visa authorities when recording a visa application and making a corresponding decision, which are transmitted to the C-VIS.
The visa authorities may copy the fingerprints in a C-VIS application data file and enter them in a new application data file. They become owner of the new data file compiled thereby.

The visa authorities may establish or delete links between application data files where the applicant belongs to a group of travellers or to a family travelling together under Article 8 paragraph 4 of the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. .

The Swiss authority recording the data of an application data file may link them with other data records relating to the same applicant in accordance with Article 8 paragraph 3 the EU VIS Regulation or the delete the corresponding links.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following authorities may consult C-VIS data online in order to fulfil the duties assigned to them:
at SEM:

item.p: the Entry Section and the Admission and Residence Section: to fulfil their tasks in relation to visas,

the Dublin Sections and the employees in reception and processing centres responsible for assessing applications for asylum: to determine the Dublin state responsible for assessing an asylum application,
the Asylum Division: to assess asylum applications where Switzerland is responsible for deciding,

the State Secretariat, the Consular Directorate and the Directorate of Political Affairs of the FDFA: to assess visa applications for which the FDFA is responsible;

blockList.listIntroduction:
the Border Guard and the responsible cantonal and communal police authorities:
Amended by No I of the O of 19 Feb. 2020, in force since 1 April 2020 (AS 2020 917).

item.p: to conduct checks at the external borders of the Schengen area and on the sovereign territory of Switzerland,
to verify the identity of visa holders, to assess the authenticity of visas or to assess whether the requirements for entry into the sovereign territory of Switzerland or for residence there are met,
in order to identify persons without visas who do not or no longer meet the requirements for entry into the sovereign territory of Switzerland or for the residence there;
the cantonal migration authorities and the communes to which the corresponding competences have been delegated by the cantons: to fulfil their duties in relation to visas.

content.p: The fedpol Operations Centre (fedpol OC) may consult C-VIS data online as central access point (Art. 20).
The rights to consult data are regulated in Annex 3.

section.heading: Data Categories for Consulting the C-VIS and Extent of Rights to Consult Data

article.heading: Consultation to assess visa applications and for visa decisions

blockList.listIntroduction:
The consultation of the C-VIS to assess visa applications and for visa decisions is carried out in accordance with Article 15 paragraph 2 the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. on the basis of one or more of the following data:

item.p: application number;
first name, surname, name at birth (previous surname), sex, and date, place and country of birth;
nature and number of the travel documents, issuing authority, date of issue and expiry date;

first name, surname and address of the natural person or name and address of the legal entity issuing the invitation or that is required to bear the subsistence costs of the visa applicant during the stay, and the first name, surname and address of the contact person for the legal entity;
fingerprints;
the number of the visa vignette and date of issue of previously issued visas.

content.p: If the search produces a hit, the authority may consult the previous application data files for the applicant under Article 15 paragraph 3 of the EU VIS Regulation and the linked application data files under Article 8 paragraph 4 of the EU VIS Regulation.

article.heading: Consultation during checks on the Schengen external borders or on Swiss sovereign territory

content.p:
The consultation of the C-VIS during checks at crossing points on the external borders of the Schengen area in order to verify the identity of the visa holder or the authenticity of the visa or to assess whether the requirements for entry into Schengen area are met is carried out in accordance with Article 18 paragraph 1 EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. on the basis of the visa vignette number and the visa holder's fingerprints.
If the search produces a hit, the authority may under Article 18 paragraph 4 EU VIS Regulation consult the data in categories I, II and V–VII in accordance with Annex 3.

The consultation of the C-VIS to verify the identity of the visa holder or the authenticity of the visa or to assess whether the requirements for entry into Swiss sovereign territory or for residence there are met is carried out in accordance with Article 19 paragraph 1 EU VIS Regulation on the basis of the visa vignette number and the visa holder's fingerprints or solely on the basis of the visa vignette number.
If the search produces a hit, the authority may under Article 19 paragraph 2 EU VIS Regulation consult the data in the categories mentioned in paragraph 2.

item.p: the verification of the identity of a visa holder under Article 13 was not successfully;
there is doubt as to the identity of the visa holder or the authenticity of the visa or of the travel documents;
the identity of a person without a visa must be verified.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the consultation on the basis of fingerprints is not successful or if it cannot be used, a consultation on the basis of the following data may be carried out:

item.p: first name, surname, name at birth (previous surname), sex, and date, place and country the birth; or
nature and number of the travel documents, issuing authority, date of issue and expiry date.

content.p: The consultation under paragraph 2 may be carried out in combination with current nationality or nationality at birth.
If the search produces a hit, the authority may under Article 20 paragraph 2 EU VIS Regulation consult the data in categories I–VII in accordance with Annex 3.

article.heading: Consultation to determine the responsible Dublin state

content.p:
The consultation of the C-VIS to determine the responsible Dublin state in accordance with Articles 12 and 34 of Regulation (EC) No 604/2013
Regulation (EU) No 604/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council 26 June 2013 establishing the criteria and mechanisms for determining the Member State responsible for examining an application for international protection lodged in one of the Member States by a third-country national or a stateless person (recast), version in accordance with OJ L 180 of 29.6.2013, p. 31. (EU Dublin-Ordinance) is carried out on the basis of the asylum seeker's fingerprints.
If the consultation on the basis of the fingerprints is unsuccessful or cannot be used, the consultation may be carried out in accordance with the procedure under Article 14 paragraphs 2 and 3.

If the search produces a hit and if a visa has been issued or extended that expired no later than six months before the date on which the asylum application was filed, the data in categories I, II, VI and VII in accordance with Annex 3 may be consulted in accordance with Article 21 paragraph 2 the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. .
Only applications that are linked due to the applicants belonging to the same family may be consulted.
The consultation of the C-VIS to assess an asylum application is carried out on the basis of the asylum seeker's fingerprints.
If the consultation on the basis of the fingerprints is unsuccessful or cannot be used, the consultation may be carried out in accordance with the procedure under Article 14 paragraphs 2 and 3.

If the search produces a hit and if a visa has been issued, the data in categories I, II and V–VII in accordance with Annex 3 may be consulted in accordance with Article 22 paragraph 2 the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. .
Only applications that are linked due to the applicants belonging to the same family may be consulted, together with the various related application data files for the same applicant.

section.heading: Access to C-VIS via the Central Access Point

article.heading: Federal authorities that may request data

blockList.listIntroduction: The following federal authorities may request C-VIS data in accordance with Article 109a paragraph 3 letters a–c FNIA:
at fedpol:

item.p: the operations centre,
the Federal Criminal Police,
the International Identifications Service;

blockList.listIntroduction: at the Federal Intelligence Service:

item.p: the Procurement Section,
the Evaluation Section,
Counter Terrorism Coordination,
Intelligence Service Coordination,
Counter Extremism Coordination,
Non-Proliferation Coordination,
the Aliens Division;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2021, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 735).

blockList.listIntroduction: at the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland:

item.p:
the Judgment Enforcement Service: to implement the decisions of the federal criminal justice authorities, unless the cantons have jurisdiction, in particular in application of Article 82 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance of 24 October 2007
SR 142.201 on Admission, Period of Stay and Employment,

the divisions conducting proceedings in Bern, namely National Security and Organised Crime, White-Collar Crime, Mutual Legal Assistance, Terrorism, International Criminal Law and Cybercrime, and the offices in Lausanne, Lugano and Zurich: for the investigation and indictment of offences that are subject to federal jurisdiction in accordance with Articles 23 and 24 of the Criminal Procedure Code
SR 312.0 or other specific federal acts.

article.heading: Cantonal and communal authorities that may request data

blockList.listIntroduction: The following cantonal and communal authorities may request C-VIS data in accordance with Article 109a paragraph 3 letter d FNIA:

item.p: the cantonal police authorities;
the communal police authorities in the cities of Zurich, Winterthur, Lausanne, Chiasso and Lugano;
the prosecution authorities via the cantonal police authorities.

content.p: The authorities under Articles 17 and 18 shall submit an application for access to the C-VIS data with a statement of the grounds to fedpol OC in paper form or electronically.

In urgent exceptional cases, an authority may also submit an application verbally. The fedpol OC shall process the application immediately and assess subsequently whether the requirements under Article 20 have been met and whether it is actually an urgent exceptional case. Retrospective assessment must be carried out immediately after the application is processed.
Fedpol set out the modalities of the procedure in processing regulations.

blockList.listIntroduction: The fedpol OC shall assess whether:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2021, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 735).
item.p: the data are required to prevent, disclose or investigate terrorist or other serious offences;
their transmission are justified in the specific case;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 10 Nov. 2021, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 735).
item.p: there are justified grounds to assume that their transmission will considerably assist in preventing, disclosing or investigating terrorist or other serious offences.

article.heading: Consultation and transmission of the data

content.p:
If the requirements under Article 20 are met, the fedpol OC shall consult the C-VIS data. The consultation may be carried out only on the basis of the data specified in Article 5 paragraph 2 of Decision 2008/633/JHA
Council Decision 2008/633/JHA of 23 June 2008 concerning access for consultation of the Visa Information System (VIS) by designated authorities of Member States and by Europol for the purposes of the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and of other serious criminal offences, version in accordance with OJ L 218 of 13.8.2008, p. 129. (EU VIS Decision) and in accordance with the rights to consult data set out in Annex 3.
If the consultation produces a hit, the fedpol OC shall transmit the data specified in Article 5 paragraph 3 of the EU VIS Decision to the authority by secure means.

article.heading: Exchange of information with EU member states not bound by the EU VIS Regulation

content.p:
The EU member states where the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. is not in force may submit applications to obtain C-VIS data either directly to the fedpol OC via the secure connections intended for criminal police correspondence or to the other authorities in accordance with Articles 17 and 18.
The fedpol OC shall assess the applications and respond to them directly.
The procedure is governed by Article 19.
The fedpol OC may, with a view to obtaining information in relation to visas, submit applications to the responsible authorities in the EU member states where the EU VIS Regulation is not in force.

chapter.heading: Consultation of Other Databases and VIS Mail

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 10 May 2023, in force since 15 June 2023 (AS 2023 246).

blockList.listIntroduction: Provided the user has the required authorisation, on receipt of a visa application in ORBIS an automatic search is made of the following databases:

item.p:
the Entry and Exit System in accordance with the Ordinance of 10 November 2021
SR 142.206 on the Entry and Exit System.

blockList.listIntroduction: The federal and cantonal visa authorities and the communal authorities to which the related competences have been delegated shall use VIS Mail to transmit the following forms of information:

item.p: communications on incorrect data in the C-VIS under Article 24 paragraph 2 EU VIS Regulation;
a notice under Article 25 paragraph 2 EU VIS Regulation that an applicant has acquired the citizenship of a Schengen state;

item.num:
d.
Inserted by No I of the O of 28 Oct. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 4235).

e.
Inserted by No I of the O of 28 Oct. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 4235).
item.p: information about visas that are issued by consulates under Article 31 paragraph 1 of the Visa Code and Article 16 paragraph 3 der EU VIS Regulation to citizens of certain countries of origin or certain groups of citizens.

chapter.heading: Data Protection, Data Security and Supervision

content.p: Only Swiss authorities may modify the data that they transmit to C-VIS.
The ORBIS data shall be stored for a maximum of five years.

blockList.listIntroduction: This period begins:

item.p: in the case of the issue of a visa: on the day that the term of validity expires;
in the case of the extension of a visa: on the day that new term of validity expires;
in the event of the withdrawal of the application or the termination or non-continuation of the assessment of an application: on the creation of the application data file in ORBIS;
in the event that a visa is refused, annulled or revoked: with the corresponding decision of the visa authority.

blockList.listIntroduction: If a person acquires Swiss citizenship:

item.p: the visa authorities shall immediately delete the application data files in ORBIS relating to the person concerned and if applicable the links with data records of his or her spouse, children or the group with which he or she travelled, provided the application data were recorded by the Swiss authorities;
SEM shall give immediate notice of this to the Schengen states that recorded the visa data.

content.p: The citizenship authorities must notify SEM (Visa Principles Section) of the naturalisation.

If the decision to refuse a visa is overturned by the competent appellate authority, the data on the refusal of the visa in ORBIS shall be deleted by the authority that refused the visa as soon as the appeal decision is final.

If there are indications that C-VIS data or ORBIS data recorded by the Swiss authorities are incorrect or incomplete or have been processed unlawfully, SEM must be notified of this immediately in writing.
SEM shall take the required action immediately.

article.heading: Storing the data from the C-VIS

content.p:
In accordance with Article 30 EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. , C-VIS data may be stored in ZEMIS, in ORBIS, in the RUMACA information system of the Border Guard or in corresponding information systems of the cantonal and communal police authorities if storage is required in the specific case and for as long as the relevant case is being processed.
Amended by No I of the O of 19 Feb. 2020, in force since 1 April 2020 (AS 2020 917).

The authorities under Articles 17 and 18 must immediately destroy the data received from the fedpol OC unless they are required for the purposes of the EU VIS Decision
See footnote to Art. 21 para. 1. . They must destroy the data as soon as they are no longer required.
Any use of data in contravention of paragraphs 1 and 2 constitutes an abuse as defined in Article 120d FNIA.

article.heading: Disclosure of data to third countries or international organisations

content.p: The C-VIS data may neither be disclosed to third countries nor to international organisations.

blockList.listIntroduction:
The following C-VIS data about a person may be disclosed to third countries or international organisations in accordance with the Annex to the EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. in specific cases in order to prove the identity of a citizen of a third country, including for the purpose of repatriation, if the conditions under Article 31 the EU VIS Regulation are fulfilled:

item.p: first name, surname, name at birth, sex, and date, place and country of birth;
current nationality and nationality at birth;
type and number of the travel documents, issuing authority, date of issue and expiry date;
applicant's home address;
for minors: first name and surname of the person holding custody or of the guardian.

content.p: The ORBIS data that are not transmitted to the C-VIS may be disclosed in the specific case in accordance with the conditions set out in Article 105 FNIA.

article.heading: Right to information or to correction or deletion of data

content.p:
If a person asserts his or her right to information in relation to data in ORBIS or in the C-VIS, he or she must submit an application to SEM in the form required by Article 16 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 August 2022
SR 235.11 (DPO). The assertion of other rights by the data subject is governed by Article 41 of the Data Protection Act of 25 September 2020
SR 235.1 .
Amended by Annex 2 No II 7 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).
SEM shall process the request for information in consultation with the authority that recorded the data in ORBIS, or with the state that transmitted the data to the C-VIS.
It shall register the request for information.

If a person asserts his or her right to the correction or deletion of C-VIS data that were not recorded by the Swiss authorities, SEM must contact the state that recorded the data within 14 days and must transmit the application to it. SEM shall notify the person concerned of the transmission of the application.
It shall process requests for information, correction or deletion immediately.
It shall immediately confirm to the person concerned in writing that it has corrected or deleted the data. If it is not prepared to correct or delete the data, it shall provide reasons for this.

blockList.listIntroduction:
When procuring personal data on the applicant, including biometric data, the applicant shall be notified in writing of the following:
Amended by Annex 2 No II 7 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).

item.num:
a.
Amended by Annex 2 No II 7 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).
item.p: the identity and contact details of the data controller;
the purpose of processing the data in ORBIS and in the C-VIS;

item.num:
c.
Amended by Annex 2 No II 7 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).
item.p: the recipients or the categories of recipient to whom their personal data will be disclosed;
the duration of the storage of data in ORBIS and in the C-VIS;
that the recording of the data is required to assess the application;
that he or she has a right to information, correction and deletion, the procedure for asserting these rights and how to contact the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).

content.p: The natural person or legal entity that has invited the applicant or must bear the costs of subsistence during his or her stay shall also receive the information under paragraph 1.

Liability for loss or damage in connection with the operation of ORBIS is governed by the Government Liability Act of 14 March 1958
SR 170.32 , and in particular by its Articles 19a–19c, which apply mutatis mutandis.

section.heading: Data Security, Advice on Data Protection and Supervision of Data Processing

blockList.listIntroduction: Data security is governed by:

item.num:
a.
Amended by Annex 2 No II 7 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).

b.
Amended by Annex 2 No II 5 of the Information Security Ordinance of 8 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 735).

c.
Repealed by Annex No 4 of the O of 24 Feb. 2021, with effect from 1 April 2021 (AS 2021 132).

content.p: In order to fulfil its statutory duties, SEM shall periodically compile statistics based on the data recorded in ORBIS.
It shall publish the most important statistics.
On request, it may provide authorities, private individuals or organisations with additional statistics that they require.
In consultation with the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, it may also compile statistics on the C-VIS. The access rights for this purpose are specified in Annex 3 adopted.
The statistics may not permit conclusions to be drawn as to the persons concerned.

The data protection officer for the FDJP shall provide support to ensure compliance with the data protection regulations. He or she shall coordinate with the federal offices involved so that they fulfil their duties under paragraph 2.
Amended by No II of the O of 2 Sept. 2015, in force since 1 Oct. 2015 (AS 2015 3047).

blockList.listIntroduction: The data protection officers for the federal offices involved shall in their particular field ensure:

item.p: that the persons processing data are properly informed;
that these persons are properly trained;
that the required checks are carried out;
that defects are rectified rapidly;
that the FDJP data protection officer is notified of the need for coordination.

content.p: The cantonal data protection authorities and the FDPIC shall work together within the limits of their respective responsibilities and coordinate supervision of the processing of personal data.
The FDPIC shall work with the European Data Protection Commissioner in fulfilling his duties; it is the national contact point for such matters.

It is the national authority under Article 41 paragraph 1 EU VIS Regulation
See footnote to Art. 2 let. a. and Articles 8 paragraph 5 and 11 EU VIS Decision
See footnote to Art. 21 para. 1. . It is responsible for fulfilling the duties set out in these articles.

The Visa Information System Ordinance of 6 July 2011
[AS 2011 3861, 4379, 4451] is repealed.
The amendment of another enactment is regulated in Annex 4.
This Ordinance comes into force on 20 January 2014.
